name: TB303 madness
description: 128 BPM | E minor | 224 bars | 7:00. Acid techno developed from TB303 Demo. 0:00 ignition; 1:00 core groove; 2:00 escalation; 3:00 bell breakdown and rebuild; 4:00 main return; 5:00 madness peak; 6:00 release and outro. Finite arrangement; final four bars reserved for decay. Original TB303 velocity-coded accent/slide, analog drums, FM bell and restored delay return. Intermittent Undertow Motion Pad: Gmaj7–F# half-diminished7–Cmaj7–Bm7, roots G4–F#4–C4–B3, two bars per chord; stereo send to Reverb Effect. Warm passages: bars 49–64, 81–88, 97–112, 145–160, 169–176, 201–216.

patchDefinitions.name: The Real TB303
patchDefinitions.description:
Sawtooth TB-303 bass with Accent and Slide implemented via midi note velocity.
Velocity selects flags only; there is no continuous velocity gain. 
- MIDI velocity 1-63: normal
-  64-95: slide
- 96-111: accent
- 112-127: accent + slide. 
Accent changes iamp from 0.4 to 0.9 and filter-envelope amount from 0.4 to 0.8.
MIDI controllers: CC10: cutoff 40-16000 Hz, logarithmic (49 approximately 404 Hz). CC11: resonance 0-0.98 (114 approximately 0.88). Both controllers follow the played MIDI channel and use 10 ms smoothing.
Performance controller iamp / Drive: 0.1-32x, logarithmic, default 1x. Multiplies the original accent-dependent iamp before tanh; new notes read the performance knob.
Slide: portk half-time 60 ms versus 1 ms for regular notes, retaining the prior voice state. For reliable previous-note glide use a single-note line, begin with a non-slide note, and leave at least 50 ms after note-off for voice reuse; overlapping/release-tail voices do not share pitch history. This is the native portk implementation, not a legato note-priority engine.
Route Stereo Output through the performance mixer to Master.
Drive output compensation: post-tanh gain (1 + 0.025 * drive) / (1.025 * drive). The 1x sound is unchanged; higher Drive primarily adds distortion with only a small level increase (approximately +1.4 dB RMS at 32x in the reference phrase). This is a fixed compensation curve, not a loudness limiter; level response varies with notes and filter settings.

patchDefinitions.name: Analog Drumkit
patchDefinitions.description: Five velocity-sensitive analog synthesis voices selected by MIDI notnum through Switch. MIDI notenum 35: Bass drum (pitch-swept sine + click); 36: Bass drum distorted (saturated sine + click); 46: Hi-hat open (700 ms); 42: Hi-hat closed (85 ms); 38: Snare (two sine resonances + filtered noise). Hats use six inharmonic square oscillators plus noise. One-shot decays survive short MIDI note-offs. Silent default; stereo output; no samples. GM bass-drum slot 36 is used for the distorted variation.

patchDefinitions.name: Delay Effect
patchDefinitions.description: Delay with multiple taps, distributed between left and right stereo channels

patchDefinitions.name: Reverb Effect
patchDefinitions.description: Stereo reverb effect, uses inleta channel names "left" and "right".

patchDefinitions.name: Undertow Motion Pad
patchDefinitions.description: Dark triangle and PWM pulse pad. Sine LFO moves pulse width from 0.32 to 0.68 and filter cutoff from 70% to 130% of Tone. Motion is Hz, not tempo sync. Suggested MIDI notes 43–79. Dry, velocity-sensitive, polyphonic. Three per-instance controls read on new notes. Route Stereo Output through the performance mixer to Master.
